extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners, USCIS adjudicators, and nonimmigrant petitioners (U, F, M, J) and their representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for SEVIS fee treatment and for filing, evidentiary, biometric, adjudicative, confidentiality, and derivative-family rules governing U-1 (victim) nonimmigrant petitions and Form I-918, Supplement A filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new SEVIS fee for certain subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who has previously paid a SEVIS fee is not required to pay a new fee in connection with: (i) an application for an extension of stay as provided in 8 CFR 214.2(f)(7) or (m)(10); (ii) an application for transfer as provided in 8 CFR 214.2(f)(8) or (m)(11); (iii) a change in educational level as provided in 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii); or (iv) an application for post-completion practical training as provided in 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii) or (m)(14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the specific categories of student/visitor benefit filings for which a previously paid SEVIS fee need not be repaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new SEVIS fee for J-1 program extension/transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: A J-1 nonimmigrant is not required to pay a new fee in connection with (i) an application for an extension of program as provided in 22 CFR 62.43; or (ii) an application for transfer of program as provided in 22 CFR 62.42.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies analogous exceptions for J-1 exchange visitors distinct from F/M student provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee not required for visa issuance for continuation of study
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1, F-3, J-1, M-1, or M-3 nonimmigrant who has previously paid the fee is not required to pay a new fee to be granted a visa to return to the United States as a continuing student or exchange visitor in a single course of study, provided the nonimmigrant is not otherwise required to pay a new fee under other provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to returning continuing students/exchange visitors; other fee-triggering circumstances can override this exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee for certain intra-student-classification changes
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee is required for changes between the F-1 and F-3 classifications, and no fee is required for changes between the M-1 and M-3 classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple classification switches between main and concomitant classifications exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary waiver for institutional reclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS retains discretionary authority to waive the additional fee requirement when a nonimmigrant changes classification between F and M if the change of status is due solely to institutional reclassification by SEVP during that nonimmigrant's course of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is discretionary and limited to institutional reclassification circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: No SEVIS fee for re-application after consular denial (12 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who fully paid a SEVIS fee in connection with an initial visa application (F-1, F-3, M-1, M-3, or J-1 in a particular program category) whose initial application was denied, and who is reapplying for the same status or category within 12 months following the initial notice of denial, is not required to repay the SEVIS fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-limited (12 months) protection for consular denials when reapplying for same status/category.

rubrics_metrics.name: No SEVIS fee for re-application after change-of-status denial and timely motion to reopen
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonimmigrant who fully paid a SEVIS fee in connection with an initial application for a change of status to F-1/F-3/M-1/M-3 or a particular J-1 category, whose initial application was denied, and who is granted a motion to reopen the denied case is not required to repay the SEVIS fee if the motion to reopen is granted within 12 months of receipt of initial notice of denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects applicants who successfully obtain reopening within 12 months from having to repay the SEVIS fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for payment of the SEVIS fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien subject to payment may pay the fee by any procedure approved by DHS, including: (i) submission of Form I-901 by mail with proper fee (check/money order/foreign draft) per 8 CFR 103.7(d)(8); (ii) electronic submission using a credit card or other DHS-accepted electronic means; or (iii) via a designated payment service and receipt mechanism approved and set forth in future DHS guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies accepted payment channels and anticipates designated third-party payment services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipts for SEVIS fee payments
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will provide a receipt for each fee payment until DHS issues a Federal Register notice that paper receipts are no longer necessary. Further provisions: (i) expedited delivery of the receipt available upon request and additional fee; (ii) if payment made electronically, DHS and DOS will accept properly completed electronic printouts in lieu of the DHS-generated receipt; (iii) if payment made through an approved payment service, DHS and DOS will accept properly completed payment-service receipts in lieu of DHS-generated receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipts may be obtained electronically or via payment service; expedited delivery available for a fee; paper receipts may be phased out by notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic record of SEVIS fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will maintain an electronic record of payment for the alien as verification of receipt. If DHS records indicate fee has been paid, an alien who has lost or did not receive a receipt will not be denied an immigration benefit solely because of failure to present a paper receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic records serve as authoritative proof of payment for adjudications and visa issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party SEVIS fee payments allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will accept payment of the required fee for an alien from a certified school or a designated exchange visitor program sponsor, or from another source, in accordance with procedures approved by DHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits institutions, sponsors, or other approved third parties to pay the fee for the alien under DHS procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay SEVIS fee grounds for denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to pay the required fee is grounds for denial of F, M, or J nonimmigrant status or status-related benefits. Payment of the fee does not preserve lawful status if the nonimmigrant has otherwise violated status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpayment is a standalone ground for denial; paying fee doesn't cure other status violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay treated as 'willful violation' for F/M reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of reinstatement to F or M status, failure to pay the required fee will be considered a 'willful violation' under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(16) or (m)(16), unless DHS determines there are sufficient extenuating circumstances (at SEVP's discretion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay can bar reinstatement absent DHS-excused extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay not 'minor or technical infraction' for J reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of reinstatement to valid J program status, failure to pay the required fee will not be considered a 'minor or technical infraction' under 22 CFR 62.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter treatment for J program participants—nonpayment is more serious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Certifying agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A certifying agency means a Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency, prosecutor, judge, or other authority that has responsibility for the investigation or prosecution of a qualifying crime or criminal activity; includes agencies with criminal investigative jurisdiction including child protective services, EEOC, Department of Labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines which entities may issue law enforcement certifications (Form I-918, Supplement B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Certifying official
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifying official means (i) the head of the certifying agency, or any supervisor specifically designated by the head to issue U certifications on behalf of that agency; or (ii) a Federal, State, or local judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only officials with specified authority may sign Supplement B certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Qualifying crime or qualifying criminal activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes one or more of the listed offenses (rape; torture; trafficking; incest; domestic violence; sexual assault; abusive sexual contact; prostitution; sexual exploitation; female genital mutilation; being held hostage; peonage; involuntary servitude; slave trade; kidnapping; abduction; unlawful criminal restraint; false imprisonment; blackmail; extortion; manslaughter; murder; felonious assault; witness tampering; obstruction of justice; perjury; or attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit any such offenses) or 'any similar activity' substantially similar in nature and elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both a non-exhaustive enumerated list and a 'substantially similar' catch-all for qualifying criminal activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Qualifying family member
rubrics_metrics.description: For an alien victim 21 or older eligible for U status, qualifying family member means the spouse or child(ren); for a victim under 21, it means spouse, child(ren), parents, or unmarried siblings under 18 of such an alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who may qualify for derivative U-2/U-3/U-4/U-5 status depending on principal's age at eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: U nonimmigrant status certification (Supplement B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means Form I-918, Supplement B, 'U Nonimmigrant Status Certification,' which confirms that the petitioner has been helpful, is being helpful, or is likely to be helpful in the investigation or prosecution of the qualifying criminal activity of which he or she is a victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must be completed by an authorized certifying official and is a key piece of initial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Victim of qualifying criminal activity — family & witness-tampering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Victim generally means an alien who has suffered direct and proximate harm due to qualifying criminal activity. (i) The alien spouse, children under 21, and if the direct victim is deceased or incompetent, parents and unmarried siblings under 18 are considered victims. (ii) A petitioner may be considered a victim of witness tampering, obstruction, or perjury if: (A) the petitioner has been directly and proximately harmed by the perpetrator; and (B) reasonable grounds exist that the perpetrator committed the offense in part to avoid/frustrate investigation/prosecution or to further abuse/exploitation/undue control through legal-system manipulation. (iii) A person culpable for the qualifying criminal activity is excluded from recognition as a victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who counts as a victim for derivative status and recognizes witness-tampering harms while excluding perpetrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Physical or mental abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Means injury or harm to the victim's physical person, or harm to or impairment of the emotional or psychological soundness of the victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the substantial-abuse eligibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criterion: Substantial physical or mental abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The alien has suffered substantial physical or mental abuse as a result of being a victim of qualifying criminal activity. Whether abuse is substantial is based on factors including but not limited to: the nature of the injury; the severity of the perpetrator's conduct; the severity of the harm suffered; the duration of infliction; and the extent of permanent or serious harm to appearance, health, or physical/mental soundness. No single factor is prerequisite; a series of acts taken together may constitute substantial abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multifactor, non-exhaustive test; no single factor is determinative and cumulative conduct may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criterion: Possession of credible and reliable information
rubrics_metrics.description: The alien possesses credible and reliable information establishing knowledge of the details concerning the qualifying criminal activity upon which the petition is based. Petitioner must possess specific facts that led the certifying official to determine the petitioner has been/is/likely to provide assistance. If under 16 at time of act, parent/guardian/next friend may possess the information; similarly for incapacitated or incompetent petitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires concrete, case-specific factual knowledge—not merely suspicion or hearsay—and allows surrogate knowledge for certain minors/incapacitated petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criterion: Helpful to law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The alien has been helpful, is being helpful, or is likely to be helpful to a certifying agency in the investigation or prosecution of the qualifying criminal activity, and since initiation of cooperation has not refused or failed to provide information and assistance reasonably requested. If under 16 at the time of the act, a parent/guardian/next friend may provide required assistance; same for incapacitated petitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement centers on cooperation; prior or prospective helpfulness qualifies, with ability to substitute assistance by guardian/next friend in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criterion: Location or extraterritorial jurisdiction of crime
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualifying criminal activity must have occurred in the United States (including Indian country and U.S. military installations) or in U.S. territories/possessions, or violated a U.S. federal law that provides for extraterritorial jurisdiction to prosecute the offense in a U.S. federal court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits qualifying offenses to U.S.-linked jurisdictional contexts or federal extraterritorial statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing: USCIS sole jurisdiction and form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS has sole jurisdiction over all petitions for U nonimmigrant status. An alien seeking U-1 nonimmigrant status must submit a Petition for U Nonimmigrant Status on the form prescribed by USCIS (Form I-918) and initial evidence in accordance with paragraph (c)(1) and the form instructions. A petitioner who received interim relief is not required to submit initial evidence with Form I-918 if relying on the law enforcement certification and other evidence submitted with the request for interim relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates Form I-918 filing with USCIS and notes exception for those with prior interim-relief submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for petitioners in removal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien in removal proceedings under section 240 or in exclusion/deportation proceedings must file Form I-918 directly with USCIS. ICE counsel may, as a matter of discretion and at the alien's request, file a joint motion to terminate proceedings without prejudice with the immigration judge or Board while the petition is adjudicated by USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides path for applicants in immigration court; ICE discretion may facilitate termination of proceedings during adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by petitioners subject to final orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien subject to a final order of removal, deportation, or exclusion is not precluded from filing a petition for U-1 directly with USCIS. Filing has no effect on ICE's authority to execute a final order, though the alien may file a request for a stay of removal. If in detention, the time during which a stay is in effect will extend the period of detention reasonably necessary to effect removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing does not automatically halt removal; separate stay request required to delay execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial evidence required with Form I-918
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-918 must include: (i) Form I-918, Supplement B signed by a certifying official within six months immediately preceding filing and stating specific certification elements; (ii) any additional evidence petitioner wants USCIS to consider to establish victimization, substantial abuse, knowledge of details, helpfulness, or qualifying location/violation; (iii) a signed statement by the petitioner describing the facts of victimization (or by parent/guardian/next friend if under 16/incapacitated); and (iv) if inadmissible, Form I-192 (Application for Advance Permission to Enter as Non-Immigrant) per 8 CFR 212.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement B (law enforcement certification) within six months is mandatory; additional documentary and testimonial evidence recommended; inadmissibility requires Form I-192.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric capture requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitioners for U-1 nonimmigrant status must submit to biometric capture and pay a biometric capture fee. USCIS will notify the petitioner of the proper time and location after filing Form I-918.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biometrics are mandatory for adjudication and require a separate fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden shall be on the petitioner to demonstrate eligibility for U-1 status. The petitioner may submit any credible evidence. USCIS shall conduct a de novo review of all evidence submitted and may investigate any aspect of the petition. Previously submitted evidence may be used but USCIS will not be bound by prior factual determinations. USCIS will determine the evidentiary value of previously or concurrently submitted evidence, including Supplement B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner bears burden; flexible admissibility of 'credible evidence'; USCIS conducts fresh, independent review and is not constrained by prior findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision: written notice and inclusion of nongovernmental resources upon approval
rubrics_metrics.description: After de novo review USCIS will issue a written decision approving or denying Form I-918 and notify the petitioner. USCIS will include in an approval decision a list of nongovernmental organizations to which the petitioner can refer regarding options and available resources while in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals include referrals to victim-service NGOs as part of relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval effects for petitioners within and outside the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS approves Form I-918 for a petitioner within the United States, USCIS will concurrently grant U-1 status and notify the alien on Form I-797 with Form I-94 indicating U-1 status. For petitioners outside the United States, USCIS will notify the alien on Form I-797 and forward notice to the Department of State for delivery to the relevant U.S. Embassy/Consulate or appropriate port of entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different operational processes for in-country vs overseas approvals; I-797/I-94 issuance for in-country approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial procedures and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will provide written notification of reasons for denial. The petitioner may appeal a denial to the Administrative Appeals Office (AAO) per 8 CFR 103.3. For petitioners who appeal to the AAO, the denial is not administratively final until AAO decision. Upon USCIS' final denial for a petitioner whose proceedings were terminated under 214.14(c)(1)(i), DHS may file a new Notice to Appear. For petitioners subject to a stay of removal, USCIS' denial will lift the stay automatically when administratively final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial includes written reasons and appellate rights; adverse effects on stays/terminations of removal proceedings possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accordance of U-1 status for petitioners previously granted U interim relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners who were granted U interim relief and whose Form I-918 is approved will be accorded U-1 status as of the date that a request for U interim relief was initially approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim-relief beneficiaries get retroactive recognition of U-1 status upon approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization incident to U-1 status
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien granted U-1 status is employment authorized incident to status. USCIS will automatically issue an initial Employment Authorization Document (EAD) to such aliens who are in the United States. For principal aliens who applied from outside the United States, the initial EAD will not be issued until the petitioner has been admitted to the United States in U status. No additional fee is required. Renewal or replacement of expiring/lost EADs requires filing Form I-765 per form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorization is an incident of status; in-country principals receive automatic EAD; overseas principals receive EAD only post-admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual numerical cap on U-1 nonimmigrant status
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of aliens who may be issued a U-1 nonimmigrant visa or granted U-1 status may not exceed 10,000 in any fiscal year (section 214(p)(2) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates numerical limitation triggering waiting-list procedures when cap reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiting list procedures when annual cap reached
rubrics_metrics.description: All eligible petitioners not granted U-1 status due solely to the cap must be placed on a waiting list and receive written notice. Priority on the waiting list is by filing date (oldest first). In the next fiscal year, USCIS will issue a number to each petition on the waiting list, in order of priority, provided the petitioner remains admissible and eligible. After issuing numbers to qualifying petitioners on the waiting list, remaining numbers for that fiscal year will be issued to new petitioners in the order properly filed. USCIS will grant deferred action or parole and may authorize employment for U-1 petitioners and qualifying family members while on the waiting list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the ordering, notification, and possible interim benefits (deferred action/parole, employment authorization) for petitioners placed on the cap-induced waiting list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlawful presence treatment while on waiting list
rubrics_metrics.description: While a petitioner for U status who was granted deferred action or parole is on the waiting list, no accrual of unlawful presence under INA section 212(a)(9)(B) will result. However, a petitioner may be removed from the waiting list and the deferred action or parole may be terminated at USCIS discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides temporary protection from unlawful-presence accrual but subject to discretionary termination or removal from list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use and disclosure of information relating to U petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Use or disclosure (other than to sworn employees of DHS, DOJ, DOS, or bureaus/agencies of those departments for legitimate purposes) of any information relating to the beneficiary of a pending or approved U petition is prohibited unless disclosure is made: (i) by the Secretary of Homeland Security at his discretion in manner like census disclosures under 13 U.S.C. 8; (ii) by the Secretary to law enforcement officials solely for legitimate law enforcement purpose; (iii) in conjunction with judicial review protecting confidentiality; (iv) after adult petitioners/status holders provide written consent waiving restrictions; (v) to agencies providing benefits solely for eligibility determinations under 8 U.S.C. 1641(c); (vi) after a petition has been denied in a final decision; (vii) to Congressional Judiciary committee chairmen/ranking members for oversight about a closed case while protecting confidentiality and omitting personally identifying information; (viii) with prior written consent to nonprofit victim-service providers to assist in obtaining services; or (ix) to federal prosecutors to comply with constitutional obligations to provide statements by witnesses and certain other documents to defendants in pending federal criminal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates permissible disclosures and emphasizes confidentiality protections and narrow exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients of information bound by confidentiality statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies receiving information under this section, whether governmental or non-governmental, are bound by confidentiality provisions and other restrictions set out in 8 U.S.C. 1367.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds statutory confidentiality obligations on recipients of disclosed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on adverse determinations based solely on perpetrator-provided information
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials of DHS are prohibited from making adverse determinations of admissibility or deportability based on information obtained solely from the perpetrator of substantial physical or mental abuse and the criminal activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents DHS from relying solely on perpetrator statements to deny or remove victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for derivative U-2/U-3/U-4/U-5 statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: A U-1 principal alien may petition for admission of a qualifying family member in U-2 (spouse), U-3 (child), U-4 (parent of U-1 who is a child under 21), or U-5 (unmarried sibling under 18) derivative status, if accompanying or following to join the principal. A qualifying family member who committed the qualifying criminal activity in a family violence or trafficking context which established the principal's eligibility shall not be granted derivative status. To be eligible: (i) the alien for whom status is sought must be a qualifying family member per paragraph (a)(10); and (ii) the qualifying family member must be admissible to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets derivative categories and two threshold eligibility requirements; excludes perpetrators from derivative relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedures for Form I-918, Supplement A
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner for U-1 may apply for derivative U status by submitting Form I-918, Supplement A for each family member either at the same time Form I-918 is filed or later. An alien granted U-1 may apply for derivatives by submitting Supplement A for each family member. All Supplement A forms must be accompanied by initial evidence and required fees per form instructions. Supplement As filed later must include a copy of the principal's Form I-918 or a copy of the principal's Form I-94 demonstrating proof of U-1 status, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides timing flexibility but requires documentary proof of the principal's filing/status for later-filed derivative petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for qualifying family members in proceedings or with final orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying family members in removal/proceedings must file Supplement A directly with USCIS; ICE counsel may move to terminate proceedings. Family members subject to final orders may still file Supplement A directly; filing does not affect ICE's authority to execute the final order though a stay may be sought. If detained, stay time extends detention reasonably necessary to bring about removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors principal petition filing rules for derivatives; filing does not automatically halt removal without separate stay action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial evidence required for Form I-918, Supplement A
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement A must include: (i) evidence demonstrating the relationship of a qualifying family member as provided in paragraph (f)(4); and (ii) if the qualifying family member is inadmissible, Form I-192 in accordance with 8 CFR 212.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationship proof is essential; inadmissibility requires waiver application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship existence and exceptions for derivative eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as set forth in subparagraphs, the relationship between the U-1 principal and the qualifying family member must exist at the time Form I-918 was filed, must continue to exist at the time Supplement A is adjudicated, and at the time of the qualifying family member's subsequent admission. Exceptions: (i) if the principal proves he/she has become the parent of a child after Form I-918 was filed, the child shall be eligible to accompany/follow to join; (ii) if principal was under 21 when filing and filed Supplement A for an unmarried sibling under 18, USCIS will continue to consider such sibling as a qualifying family member even if the principal is no longer under 21 or sibling no longer under 18 at adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule requires contemporaneous relationship, but permits post-filing birth and certain youth-sibling exceptions tied to principal's age at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric capture and evidentiary standards apply to derivative petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions for biometric capture and evidentiary standards in paragraphs (c)(3) and (c)(4) (biometrics required; burden on petitioner; credible evidence; de novo review) also apply to petitions for qualifying family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivatives are subject to the same biometric and evidentiary rules as principal petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision procedures for Form I-918, Supplement A
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will issue written decisions approving or denying Supplement A and send notice to the U-1 principal. An approval for a qualifying family member within the United States will concurrently grant U-2/U-3/U-4/U-5 status and be notified by Form I-797 with a Form I-94. Approvals for family members outside the United States will be forwarded to the Department of State for delivery to the relevant post. Denials will include reasons and may be appealed to the AAO per 8 CFR 103.3. Upon USCIS' final denial of Supplement A for a qualifying family member whose proceedings were terminated pursuant to 214.14(f)(2)(i), DHS may file a new Notice to Appear. USCIS may include a list of nongovernmental organizations in approvals similar to principal decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels principal decision processes, including notification, appeals, possible effects on removal proceedings, and NGO referrals.
